doc.title: Onaje Allan Gumbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001

title: Learning to compose and the Fredonia contest win
summary: His piano teacher has him set Christmas-card poems to music; he never follows strict form, yet wins a Fredonia composition contest.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: talents, because at Christmas time we’d have to prepare a concert for our families, because you know they’d have a big Christmas dinner, and afterwards fill their face, you know, come and hear little Allan play a little concert. So she helped all the students prepare these concerts. And with that she would have five Christmas cards on the piano. So she would say, “Well pick one that you like.” So I looked and picked one that I thought was nice. I’d open it. And she’d say, “Okay I want you to set this poem to music.” And that’s how I started getting into composition. And along with my love for Henry Mancini, my composing talents started to develop. I never really studied formally composition. By the time I took any composition courses, I took an elective in high school and one in college, I’d already been doing it. And one thing about my composition technique, I never could follow strict forms. In other words, like following the sonata form or whatever. And I remember in high school my composition teacher in high school told me I would never become a good composer because I didn’t follow the method to a tee. They used to say when I got to Fredonia, and I entered a contest where I had written a woodwind quartet piece—
That you played on. Did you play on that?
I don’t think I played on it, I remember listening to it.
Yeah, the woodwind quartet piece, I took first place. Well it was very interesting that one of the professors, Dr. Shields
He came to the lunch room and said, “Allan won the contest, and it wasn’t even jazz.” Which was interesting because in going to Fredonia, that was kind of a culture shock.
